content.text:
I implemented `slugify(text)` in `src/strings.js` and added tests for it in `test/strings.test.js`. `npm test` passes all 13 tests: the 2 that were already there and 11 new ones for `slugify`.

How it works, in order:
1. It lowercases the text, splits accented letters into a base letter plus accent marks, and drops the accent marks. So "Tiếng Việt" becomes "tieng viet".
2. A few Latin letters don't split that way, so it maps them directly: `đ`/`ð`→`d`, `ø`→`o`, `ł`→`l`, `ß`→`ss`, `æ`→`ae`, `œ`→`oe`, `þ`→`th`. `Đ` is covered because it's lowercased to `đ` first.
3. Every run of characters other than a-z or 0-9 becomes a single `-`, and hyphens at the start and end are removed.
4. It cuts the slug to 50 characters, then removes any hyphen left at the end of the cut.

The new tests cover Vietnamese, `đ`/`Đ`, French and Spanish accents, collapsing runs of symbols, keeping digits, trimming hyphens and empty results. Three tests cover the 50-character limit, including the case where the cut lands right on a hyphen.

Only `đ`/`Đ` was in your rules; the other six letters in step 2 are my addition, so they don't disappear from the slug. Other non-Latin characters, such as Chinese or Cyrillic, are treated as separators and dropped, as your a-z/0-9 rule says.

I haven't committed anything.
